Subject: Alignment: Ridgeline inference SLAs, model profile, and ops runbook

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source-of-truth. High-level takeaway: Ridgeline needs predictable latency for inference endpoints plus a path to cost-control as load scales.

Pain points & goals we heard
- Tail latency variability during peak billing windows (user-facing product) — current spikes to ~400ms P95 on baseline model.
- Need predictable per-request SLOs for search/compose features (SLA target: P95 <= 150ms, P99 <= 400ms; final numbers below).
- Throughput: steady-state 600 RPS with 2x peak bursts (target supporting up to ~1,200 RPS for short windows).
- Data security: VPC/private deployment for PII-sensitive traffic; SOC 2 evidence required for Procurement.

Model & quality constraints
- Primary model family: 70B chat/assistant class (they mentioned a tuned Llama-derivative).
- Q&A and short-form content generation are top workload patterns; average prompt+response token count ~120 tokens.

Initial SLO proposal (for discussion)
- Latency: P50 <= 40ms, P95 <= 150ms, P99 <= 450ms (in-region hosted; private deployment may have additional network overhead).
- Throughput: baseline 600 RPS with autoscale to 1,200 RPS within 90s of sustained rise.
- Cost target: reduce per-1000-token spend by 20% vs current baseline using batching + KV cache.

Deployment topology options we discussed
1) Hosted primary + Dedicated fallback: fastest onboarding, Redwood-hosted inference with routing policy to Dedicated pool if capacity/latency degrades.
2) Dedicated-reserved GPUs in Ridgeline VPC (peered): best for isolation & constant throughput.
3) Private on-prem (future): for EU-only data residency and air-gapped workflows.

Attachments: ridgeline_slo_proposal.pdf (proposal with initial SLO curves and cost estimates).

Next steps (proposed)
- Marcus to draft a topology/ops runbook with concrete batching and cache knobs — deliver by EOD 10/06.
- Ridgeline to confirm model artifact format (HF tar / GGUF) and whether 8-bit quantized variants are acceptable.
- Triage procurement checklist: Aisha to share timelines and SOC2 contacts.

Would love a quick confirmation that these capture the call. If anything is off, reply inline and we’ll update.

—

1) Model artifacts & accuracy
- We can export in HF tar or GGUF. Preferred for inference is GGUF if Redwood supports the quantized runtime (we noted 8-bit/4-bit support requirement).
- We will provide a test prompt set (50 examples) for quality verification.

2) SLO expectations
- The product team will accept P95 <= 150ms for interactive paths, but we need the P99 to be explained (we currently see P99 spikes > 800ms). If Redwood can guarantee fallback behavior (lower-cost model) at sustained degradation, that would help our SLA commitments.

3) Compliance & procurement
- Procurement is targeting contract signature in Q4; SOC 2 Type II is required and baseline audit artifacts (logs, retention policy) will be reviewed.

Action items from our side

Internal technical breakdown (posting here so Tessa/Irène have an ops-first draft to iterate with Aisha):

Summary of feasibility vs ask
- P95 <= 150ms for a 70B chat model is achievable in-hosted mode with continuous batching + KV cache and H100 (or top-bin A100) GPUs sized to expected concurrency. For ~600 RPS baseline we recommend a pool of 6 x H100-80GB (concurrent tokens + KV) with autoscale headroom to add 4 nodes for burst to 1,200 RPS.

Key levers and default settings to hit targets
- Batching windows: 50ms target with latency-first policy; adaptive window when load increases.
- KV cache: aim for 55–65% prefix hit rate on conversational traffic — size KV per instance to hold ~3M tokens of hot context (depends on average session length).
- Quantization: prefer 4-bit quantized GGUF for cost/throughput wins if quality holds on test set; fallback path to int8 or full precision for critical calls.
- Serving topology: multi-zone Hosted with smart routing to Dedicated pool in same region. Fallback policy: when 95th-percentile across nodes >200ms for >60s, route new sessions to a smaller model variant (e.g., 13B tuned) with graceful degrade and flagged telemetry.

Network & security notes for VPC peering
- Expect ~8–12ms additional RTT for peered VPC traffic depending on cloud region — factor into P95 budget.
- Require NAT egress rules and a dedicated endpoint for telemetry ingestion (TLS).

Instrumentation & SLO verification
- Per-request tracing with distributed span id; token-level cost breakdown; daily SLO digest and 1-hour alerting on P95 breach.

Open questions for Ridgeline (need answers to size right)
- Confirmation of average active session length (in tokens) and number of concurrent users per session.
- Acceptance threshold for quality drop if fallback to 13B occurs (provide quality gate numbers).

Deliverables / next steps (internal)
- Draft runbook + topology diagram (ops-runbook-draft.md + topology-diagram.png) — targeted 10/07 morning.
- Cost projection (baseline vs with 4-bit quant) for procurement package.

Thanks everyone — finalizing the runbook and mutual action plan below. I've incorporated Marcus's notes and Aisha's constraints around procurement & SOC2.

Confirmed runbook highlights
- Baseline pool: 6 x H100-80GB (hosted) in us-west-2; autoscale policy +4 nodes for 1200 RPS peak.
- Latency SLO: P95 target 150ms (hosted), with documented network overhead for VPC peering. Fallback routing to 13B tuned variant when sustained P95>200ms for >60s.
- KV cache sizing: per-instance ~3M hot tokens; warmup strategy: pre-warm top-50 sessions on deploy.
- Quantization plan: run GGUF 4-bit on test set; if quality delta <=1.5% on key metrics, enable in prod canary.

Compliance & procurement items to attach
- SOC2 artifacts: retention policy, audit logs export (we will provide sample logs and a checklist).
- Contract draft: include SLA appendix with rollback & credit triggers for sustained breaches (we will propose specific credit terms in the procurement package).

Outstanding items for Ridgeline (Aisha/Chris)
- Provide prompt sample set and acceptance gates by 10/08.
- Confirm whether VPC peering requires egress through their NAT (affects network budget).
- Procurement: expected signature window in Q4; please share specific PO/contact so we can align legal.

Next steps / owner table
- Marcus: finalize ops-runbook-draft.md + topology-diagram.png — due 10/07 AM (DONE, attached).
- Tessa: schedule demo of canary run once we have prompt samples — target week of 10/11.
- Aisha: send prompt samples + procurement contact — due 10/08.
- Procurement: we will attach SOC2 evidence bundle to the proposal.

If that looks right, I'll push the updated runbook PDF and a brief cost appendix to the shared link.

Thanks all,
Irene Choi
